question: Where did King Solomon and all the congregation of Israel assemble at the beginning of his reign to seek the LORD, and what sacred antiquity was located there?
opt1: At the high place that was at Gibeon; for there was the tabernacle of the congregation of God, which Moses the servant of the LORD had made in the wilderness
opt2: At the ancient sanctuary of Shiloh; for there stood the stone altar of Joshua and the tent of the testimony
opt3: At Mount Gerizim in Samaria; for there was the bronze laver of Aaron and the memorial stones of Gilgal
opt4: At the threshingfloor of Ornan the Jebusite; for there David had pitched the curtain pavilion for the ark
correct: At the high place that was at Gibeon; for there was the tabernacle of the congregation of God, which Moses the servant of the LORD had made in the wilderness
explanation: Solomon convened the national leadership at Gibeon because Moses' historic wilderness Tabernacle of the Congregation and Bezaleel's bronze altar were stationed there, while the Ark resided in Jerusalem. 2 Chronicles 1:3 (KJV) - "So Solomon, and all the congregation with him, went to the high place that was at Gibeon; for there was the tabernacle of the congregation of God, which Moses the servant of the LORD had made in the wilderness."

question: What specific sacred altar stood before the tabernacle of the LORD at Gibeon upon which Solomon offered sacrifice, and who was its original craftsman?
opt1: The golden altar of incense, that Ithamar the son of Aaron had fashioned
opt2: The brasen altar, that Bezaleel the son of Uri, the son of Hur, had made
opt3: The unhewn stone altar of testimony, that Eleazar the priest had erected
opt4: The cedar altar overlaid with brass, that Hiram the artisan of Tyre had cast
correct: The brasen altar, that Bezaleel the son of Uri, the son of Hur, had made
explanation: At Gibeon stood the historic wilderness bronze altar fashioned by Bezaleel son of Uri, upon which Solomon offered his massive royal sacrifice. 2 Chronicles 1:5 (KJV) - "Moreover the brasen altar, that Bezaleel the son of Uri, the son of Hur, had made, he put before the tabernacle of the LORD: and Solomon and the congregation sought unto it."

question: How many burnt offerings did Solomon offer upon the brazen altar before the LORD at Gibeon?
opt1: Seven hundred bullocks and seven thousand sheep
opt2: Twelve hundred bullocks according to the twelve tribes of Israel
opt3: A thousand burnt offerings did Solomon offer upon that altar
opt4: Three thousand heifers and five hundred rams of consecration
correct: A thousand burnt offerings did Solomon offer upon that altar
explanation: Demonstrating magnificent royal devotion, Solomon sacrificed one thousand burnt offerings upon Bezaleel's brazen altar at Gibeon. 2 Chronicles 1:6 (KJV) - "And Solomon went up thither to the brasen altar before the LORD, which was at the tabernacle of the congregation, and offered a thousand burnt offerings upon it."

question: When God appeared to Solomon in Gibeon by night saying, 'Ask what I shall give thee', what specific request did Solomon make of the LORD?
opt1: 'Grant me long life, victory over all my foes, and the wealth of Tyre and Egypt to beautify thy sanctuary'
opt2: 'Bestow upon me the spirit of Elijah and the battle courage of my father David to subdue the heathen nations'
opt3: 'Give me an understanding heart to build thee an house of cedar and gold such as no monarch hath ever raised'
opt4: 'Give me now wisdom and knowledge, that I may go out and come in before this people: for who can judge this thy people, that is so great?'
correct: 'Give me now wisdom and knowledge, that I may go out and come in before this people: for who can judge this thy people, that is so great?'
explanation: Conscious of the immense weight of ruling God's covenant people, young Solomon humbly sought divine wisdom and discernment rather than personal longevity, riches, or military conquests. 2 Chronicles 1:10 (KJV) - "Give me now wisdom and knowledge, that I may go out and come in before this people: for who can judge this thy people, that is so great?"

question: Because Solomon asked for wisdom and knowledge to govern God's people rather than selfish pursuits, what additional gifts did God promise to grant him?
opt1: Wisdom and knowledge is granted unto thee; and I will give thee riches, and wealth, and honour, such as none of the kings have had that have been before thee, neither shall there any after thee have the like
opt2: Thou shalt have forty years of uninterrupted peace, three hundred wives of royal blood, and dominion over all Syria
opt3: I will grant thee eternal life in my presence and make thy seed to sit upon the throne of David throughout all generations
opt4: Thy borders shall extend from the Euphrates unto the ends of the earth and the gold of Sheba shall be brought unto thee daily
correct: Wisdom and knowledge is granted unto thee; and I will give thee riches, and wealth, and honour, such as none of the kings have had that have been before thee, neither shall there any after thee have the like
explanation: Because Solomon prioritized righteous stewardship over personal aggrandizement, God supernaturally bestowed unexcelled riches, wealth, and royal majesty. 2 Chronicles 1:12 (KJV) - "Wisdom and knowledge is granted unto thee; and I will give thee riches, and wealth, and honour, such as none of the kings have had that have been before thee, neither shall there any after thee have the like."

question: What military forces and vehicles did Solomon gather together, as recorded in 2 Chronicles 1:14?
opt1: Two thousand iron chariots and twenty-four thousand horsemen stationed at Hazor and Megiddo
opt2: A thousand and four hundred chariots, and twelve thousand horsemen, which he placed in the chariot cities, and with the king at Jerusalem
opt3: Eight hundred battle chariots and ten thousand cavalrymen distributed among the twelve tribal rulers
opt4: Three thousand chariots of war and thirty thousand archers stationed along the Philistine frontier
correct: A thousand and four hundred chariots, and twelve thousand horsemen, which he placed in the chariot cities, and with the king at Jerusalem
explanation: Solomon built a formidable military infrastructure consisting of 1,400 chariots and 12,000 horsemen garrisoned in designated chariot cities and Jerusalem. 2 Chronicles 1:14 (KJV) - "And Solomon gathered chariots and horsemen: and he had a thousand and four hundred chariots, and twelve thousand horsemen, which he placed in the chariot cities, and with the king at Jerusalem."

question: To what common natural items did the chronicler compare the abundance of silver, gold, and cedar wood in Jerusalem during Solomon's reign?
opt1: Silver was counted as common clay, gold as the sand of the seashore, and cedar as willow trees along the Jordan
opt2: Gold was as common dust in the streets, silver as gravel of the brook Kidron, and cedar as desert thorn bushes
opt3: The king made silver and gold at Jerusalem as plenteous as stones, and cedar trees made he as the sycomore trees that are in the vale for abundance
opt4: Silver and brass were accounted as pebbles, fine gold as autumn leaves, and cedar wood as reeds of the Nile
correct: The king made silver and gold at Jerusalem as plenteous as stones, and cedar trees made he as the sycomore trees that are in the vale for abundance
explanation: 2 Chronicles 1:15 vividly portrays the economic zenith of Solomon's kingdom, where precious metals and imported Phoenician cedar were as ubiquitous as ordinary limestone and valley sycamore trees. 2 Chronicles 1:15 (KJV) - "And the king made silver and gold at Jerusalem as plenteous as stones, and cedar trees made he as the sycomore trees that are in the vale for abundance."

question: From which country were horses and linen yarn imported for Solomon's royal merchant enterprises?
opt1: Horses were brought from the pastures of Togarmah and fine linen from the weavers of Tyre
opt2: Warhorses were procured from Cilicia and dyed fabrics from the merchants of Damascus
opt3: Chariot stallions were imported from Arabia and embroidered linen from Babylon
opt4: Solomon had horses brought out of Egypt, and linen yarn: the king's merchants received the linen yarn at a price
correct: Solomon had horses brought out of Egypt, and linen yarn: the king's merchants received the linen yarn at a price
explanation: Solomon developed an international trade monopoly, importing warhorses and fine linen yarn directly out of Egypt through royal merchants. 2 Chronicles 1:16 (KJV) - "And Solomon had horses brought out of Egypt, and linen yarn: the king's merchants received the linen yarn at a price."

question: What standard purchase prices were paid by Solomon's merchants for an imported Egyptian chariot and a horse?
opt1: Six hundred shekels of silver for a chariot, and an hundred and fifty for an horse
opt2: Four hundred shekels of silver for a chariot, and one hundred for a horse
opt3: One thousand shekels of brass for a chariot, and two hundred for a horse
opt4: Fifty shekels of gold for a chariot, and twenty shekels of gold for a horse
correct: Six hundred shekels of silver for a chariot, and an hundred and fifty for an horse
explanation: The established commercial tariff for royal imports from Egypt was 600 shekels of silver for a complete chariot unit and 150 shekels for a warhorse. 2 Chronicles 1:17 (KJV) - "And they fetched up, and brought forth out of Egypt a chariot for six hundred shekels of silver, and an horse for an hundred and fifty: and so brought they out horses for all the kings of the Hittites, and for the kings of Syria, by their means."

question: To which foreign monarchs did Solomon's royal trading agents export horses and chariots brought out of Egypt?
opt1: For the princes of the Philistines and the rulers of Ammon and Moab
opt2: For all the kings of the Hittites, and for the kings of Syria, by their means
opt3: For the monarch of Assyria and the dukes of Edom in Mount Seir
opt4: For the seafaring lords of Tyre and the chieftains of the Arabian desert
correct: For all the kings of the Hittites, and for the kings of Syria, by their means
explanation: Solomon served as the vital commercial broker between Egypt and northern powers, supplying Hittite and Aramean (Syrian) monarchs with Egyptian equine equipment. 2 Chronicles 1:17 (KJV) - "And they fetched up, and brought forth out of Egypt a chariot for six hundred shekels of silver, and an horse for an hundred and fifty: and so brought they out horses for all the kings of the Hittites, and for the kings of Syria, by their means."

question: What two major architectural building projects did King Solomon determine to execute in 2 Chronicles 2:1?
opt1: A fortified wall around Jerusalem, and an armory in the forest of Lebanon
opt2: An house for the name of the LORD, and an house for his kingdom
opt3: A judgment hall of cedar pillars, and a sanctuary tent upon Mount Zion
opt4: A water aqueduct from Bethlehem, and an ivory citadel for the daughter of Pharaoh
correct: An house for the name of the LORD, and an house for his kingdom
explanation: Solomon embarked on a dual building campaign: constructing the sacred Temple dedicated to Yahweh's name, alongside the royal palace administrative complex. 2 Chronicles 2:1 (KJV) - "And Solomon determined to build an house for the name of the LORD, and an house for his kingdom."

question: What total labor force did Solomon conscript for the preparation and transport of temple building materials in 2 Chronicles 2:2?
opt1: Fifty thousand burden-bearers, sixty thousand quarrymen, and two thousand five hundred taskmasters
opt2: One hundred thousand bearers of loads, fifty thousand stonemasons, and four thousand officers
opt3: Threescore and ten thousand men to bear burdens, and fourscore thousand to hew in the mountain, and three thousand and six hundred to oversee them
opt4: Thirty thousand timber fellers, forty thousand stone carvers, and one thousand Levite overseers
correct: Threescore and ten thousand men to bear burdens, and fourscore thousand to hew in the mountain, and three thousand and six hundred to oversee them
explanation: The building workforce numbered 70,000 burden-bearers, 80,000 mountain quarrymen, and 3,600 overseers to supervise the vast construction project. 2 Chronicles 2:2 (KJV) - "And Solomon told out threescore and ten thousand men to bear burdens, and fourscore thousand to hew in the mountain, and three thousand and six hundred to oversee them."

question: To which Phoenician king did Solomon send a diplomatic request for timber and skilled craftsmen to assist in building the temple?
opt1: Hiram the king of Sidon
opt2: Ethbaal the king of Byblos
opt3: Tabrimmon the king of Damascus
opt4: Huram the king of Tyre
correct: Huram the king of Tyre
explanation: Solomon addressed his royal requisition to Huram (Hiram) king of Tyre, recalling Huram's friendship and supply of cedars to his father David. 2 Chronicles 2:3 (KJV) - "And Solomon sent to Huram the king of Tyre, saying, As thou didst deal with David my father, and didst send him cedars to build him an house to dwell therein, even so deal with me."

question: What profound theological rationale did Solomon give to King Huram regarding the transcendent nature of the God of Israel and the temple being constructed?
opt1: 'The house which I build is great: for great is our God above all gods. But who is able to build him an house, seeing the heaven and heaven of heavens cannot contain him?'
opt2: 'The temple must surpass all sanctuaries of Babylon, for Yahweh is jealous of the shrines of Baal and Dagon'
opt3: 'No mortal hands can build a dwelling for God, yet he hath commanded us to enclose his mercy seat in cedar and bronze'
opt4: 'Our God hath chosen Zion alone among the mountains of the earth to place his eternal throne amidst thick darkness'
correct: 'The house which I build is great: for great is our God above all gods. But who is able to build him an house, seeing the heaven and heaven of heavens cannot contain him?'
explanation: Solomon confessed the utter transcendence of Yahweh to Huram, declaring that the cosmos cannot contain God, and that the temple is primarily an altar for sacred offerings. 2 Chronicles 2:5-6 (KJV) - "And the house which I build is great: for great is our God above all gods. But who is able to build him an house, seeing the heaven and heaven of heavens cannot contain him? who am I then, that I should build him an house, save only to burn sacrifice before him?"

question: What specific varieties of timber did Solomon request Huram to send from the forests of Lebanon?
opt1: Oak timbers, cypress beams, and olive wood from the northern slopes
opt2: Cedar trees, fir trees, and algum trees, out of Lebanon
opt3: Sycamore planks, acacia wood, and pine logs from Mount Hermon
opt4: Teak wood, pomegranate poles, and walnut timber from Phoenicia
correct: Cedar trees, fir trees, and algum trees, out of Lebanon
explanation: Solomon requested cedar, fir (cypress), and precious algum (sandalwood) timbers from Lebanon, known for their structural endurance and aromatic resonance. 2 Chronicles 2:8 (KJV) - "Send me also cedar trees, fir trees, and algum trees, out of Lebanon: for I know that thy servants can skill to cut timber in Lebanon; and, behold, my servants shall be with thy servants."

question: What exact agricultural supplies did Solomon pledge to give annually to Huram's woodcutters who hewed timber in Lebanon?
opt1: Ten thousand cors of fine flour, fifteen thousand measures of barley, and twelve thousand baths of pressed olive oil
opt2: Thirty thousand bushels of wheat, ten thousand measures of spelt, and five thousand skins of sweet vintage wine
opt3: Twenty thousand measures of beaten wheat, and twenty thousand measures of barley, and twenty thousand baths of wine, and twenty thousand baths of oil
opt4: Forty thousand measures of ground meal, twenty-five thousand measures of grain, and eight thousand jars of pure honey
correct: Twenty thousand measures of beaten wheat, and twenty thousand measures of barley, and twenty thousand baths of wine, and twenty thousand baths of oil
explanation: Solomon compensated Huram's timber-felling workforce with 20,000 cors of beaten wheat, 20,000 cors of barley, 20,000 baths of wine, and 20,000 baths of olive oil. 2 Chronicles 2:10 (KJV) - "And, behold, I will give to thy servants, the hewers that cut timber, twenty thousand measures of beaten wheat, and twenty thousand measures of barley, and twenty thousand baths of wine, and twenty thousand baths of oil."

question: How did King Huram of Tyre respond in writing to Solomon's request, demonstrating his reverence for Yahweh?
opt1: 'The gods of Tyre rejoice in thy wisdom, and Baal shall grant peace between our kingdoms forever'
opt2: 'Thy gold of Ophir is acceptable in our sight, and our navies shall bring thee the treasures of Tarshish'
opt3: 'David thy father was a man of war, but thou art a king of peace; therefore all Lebanon is at thy disposal'
opt4: 'Because the LORD hath loved his people, he hath made thee king over them ... Blessed be the LORD God of Israel, that made heaven and earth, who hath given to David the king a wise son'
correct: 'Because the LORD hath loved his people, he hath made thee king over them ... Blessed be the LORD God of Israel, that made heaven and earth, who hath given to David the king a wise son'
explanation: Huram's royal epistolary reply acknowledged Yahweh as the Creator of heaven and earth and traced Solomon's wise accession to God's covenant love for Israel. 2 Chronicles 2:11-12 (KJV) - "Then Huram the king of Tyre answered in writing, which he sent to Solomon, Because the LORD hath loved his people, he hath made thee king over them. Huram said moreover, Blessed be the LORD God of Israel, that made heaven and earth, who hath given to David the king a wise son, endued with prudence and understanding, that might build an house for the LORD, and an house for his kingdom."

question: What was the ancestral background of Huram-abi, the master artisan whom King Huram sent to oversee artistic metalwork and fabric weaving for Solomon?
opt1: The son of a woman of the daughters of Dan, and his father was a man of Tyre
opt2: The son of a Hebrew woman of the tribe of Asher, and his father was an artisan of Sidon
opt3: The son of a woman of the tribe of Naphtali, and his father was a bronze founder of Damascus
opt4: The son of a daughter of Judah, and his father was an Egyptian metalworker
correct: The son of a woman of the daughters of Dan, and his father was a man of Tyre
explanation: Huram-abi was born of mixed parentage—his mother belonging to the tribe of Dan (with northern ties to Naphtali) and his father being a Phoenician bronze artisan of Tyre. 2 Chronicles 2:14 (KJV) - "The son of a woman of the daughters of Dan, and his father was a man of Tyre, skilful to work in gold, and in silver, in brass, in iron, in stone, and in timber, in purple, in blue, and in fine linen, and in crimson; also to grave any manner of graving, and to find out every device which shall be put to him ..."

question: By what maritime route and to which port city did Huram propose to transport the timber rafts from Lebanon?
opt1: In barges across the Great Sea to Caesarea, and thence by oxen through the hills
opt2: In flotes by sea to Joppa; and thou shalt carry it up to Jerusalem
opt3: In rafts along the coast to Ashdod, and thence by wagon through the valley of Sorek
opt4: By sea to Tyre's southern port at Dor, and thence through the plain of Sharon
correct: In flotes by sea to Joppa; and thou shalt carry it up to Jerusalem
explanation: Lebanese timber was bound into seaworthy rafts (flotes), navigated down the Mediterranean coast, received at the port of Joppa, and hauled overland to Jerusalem. 2 Chronicles 2:16 (KJV) - "And we will cut wood out of Lebanon, as much as thou shalt need: and we will bring it to thee in flotes by sea to Joppa; and thou shalt carry it up to Jerusalem."

question: Who composed the census of 153,600 laborers conscripted by Solomon for temple construction work, as specified in 2 Chronicles 2:17?
opt1: The native Israelites drafted from the northern ten tribes under Jeroboam
opt2: The captives of war taken from the Philistines and the kingdom of Ammon
opt3: All the strangers that were in the land of Israel, after the numbering wherewith David his father had numbered them
opt4: The resident merchant families and trading guilds dwelling in Jerusalem
correct: All the strangers that were in the land of Israel, after the numbering wherewith David his father had numbered them
explanation: Solomon drew his heavy labor force of 153,600 from resident foreign aliens (strangers) living peacefully in Israel, sparing native Israelites from involuntary serfdom. 2 Chronicles 2:17-18 (KJV) - "And Solomon numbered all the strangers that were in the land of Israel, after the numbering wherewith David his father had numbered them; and they were found an hundred and fifty thousand and three thousand and six hundred. And he set threescore and ten thousand of them to be bearers of burdens, and fourscore thousand to be hewers in the mountain, and three thousand and six hundred overseers to set the people a work."

question: On which precise mountain, historic site, and calendar date did King Solomon begin building the house of the LORD in Jerusalem?
opt1: In mount Zion, where the ark rested in curtains, in the fifteenth day of the seventh month, in the third year of his reign
opt2: In mount Olivet, where David had worshipped God in weeping, in the first day of the first month, in the fifth year of his reign
opt3: In mount Moriah, where the LORD appeared unto David his father, in the place that David had prepared in the threshingfloor of Ornan the Jebusite, in the second day of the second month, in the fourth year of his reign
opt4: In mount Gibeon, where Bezaleel's altar stood, in the tenth day of the fourth month, in the second year of his reign
correct: In mount Moriah, where the LORD appeared unto David his father, in the place that David had prepared in the threshingfloor of Ornan the Jebusite, in the second day of the second month, in the fourth year of his reign
explanation: The Temple foundation was laid on Mount Moriah (where Abraham offered Isaac and God halted the destroying angel at Ornan's threshingfloor) on the second day of the second month in Solomon's fourth regnal year. 2 Chronicles 3:1-2 (KJV) - "Then Solomon began to build the house of the LORD at Jerusalem in mount Moriah, where the LORD appeared unto David his father, in the place that David had prepared in the threshingfloor of Ornan the Jebusite. And he began to build in the second day of the second month, in the fourth year of his reign."

question: What were the ground dimensions of the temple foundation according to ancient sacred cubits?
opt1: The length was an hundred cubits, and the breadth fifty cubits

explanation: According to the archaic first measure cubit, the main temple edifice measured 60 cubits in length and 20 cubits in breadth. 2 Chronicles 3:3 (KJV) - "Now these are the things wherein Solomon was instructed for the building of the house of God. The length by cubits after the first measure was threescore cubits, and the breadth twenty cubits."

question: What was the height of the monumental porch that stood before the front of the house of the LORD?
opt1: The height was an hundred and twenty: and he overlaid it within with pure gold
opt2: The height was thirty cubits, overlaid within with silver plates
opt3: The height was sixty cubits, adorned with carved palm branches
opt4: The height was forty-five cubits, crowned with bronze pomegranates
correct: The height was an hundred and twenty: and he overlaid it within with pure gold
explanation: The majestic entrance porch stood 120 cubits high, towering above the main sanctuary and fully overlaid interiorly with pure gold. 2 Chronicles 3:4 (KJV) - "And the porch that was in the front of the house, the length of it was according to the breadth of the house, twenty cubits, and the height was an hundred and twenty: and he overlaid it within with pure gold."

question: With what wood was the ceiling of the greater house adorned, and with gold from which famous source was it overlaid?
opt1: He ceiled with cedar of Lebanon, overlaid with gold of Ophir and studded with lapis lazuli
opt2: He cieled with fir tree, which he overlaid with fine gold, and he garnished the house with precious stones for beauty: and the gold was gold of Parvaim
opt3: He ceiled with olive wood, overlaid with gold of Sheba and set with carbuncles
opt4: He ceiled with algum timber, overlaid with refined gold of Uphaz and emeralds

explanation: The main sanctuary ceiling was crafted from fir wood, carved with palm trees and chains, and coated with exquisite gold of Parvaim. 2 Chronicles 3:5-6 (KJV) - "And the greater house he cieled with fir tree, which he overlaid with fine gold, and set thereon palm trees and chains. And he garnished the house with precious stones for beauty: and the gold was gold of Parvaim."

question: What were the dimensions of the Most Holy Place (the Oracle), and what quantity of fine gold was expended to overlay it?
opt1: Ten cubits square, overlaid with three hundred talents of refined gold
opt2: Thirty cubits by twenty cubits, overlaid with one thousand talents of gold of Ophir
opt3: The length thereof was according to the breadth of the house, twenty cubits, and the breadth thereof twenty cubits: and he overlaid it with fine gold, amounting to six hundred talents
opt4: Fifteen cubits cube, overlaid with four hundred and fifty talents of gold
correct: The length thereof was according to the breadth of the house, twenty cubits, and the breadth thereof twenty cubits: and he overlaid it with fine gold, amounting to six hundred talents
explanation: The Holy of Holies formed a perfect 20-cubit cube, overlaid completely with 600 talents of fine gold. 2 Chronicles 3:8 (KJV) - "And he made the most holy house, the length whereof was according to the breadth of the house, twenty cubits, and the breadth thereof twenty cubits: and he overlaid it with fine gold, amounting to six hundred talents."

question: What was the recorded weight of the golden nails used in constructing the Most Holy Place?
opt1: The weight of the nails was twenty shekels of gold

opt4: The weight of the nails was fifty shekels of gold

explanation: Even the architectural fasteners in the Holy of Holies were crafted of solid gold, with the nails weighing 50 shekels of gold. 2 Chronicles 3:9 (KJV) - "And the weight of the nails was fifty shekels of gold. And he overlaid the upper chambers with gold."

question: How were the two colossal cherubim inside the Most Holy Place constructed and positioned?
opt1: Two cherubims of image work, and overlaid them with gold ... and their faces were inward
opt2: Carved of olive trees and placed back to back facing the north and south walls
opt3: Cast of solid beaten brass and knelt facing the mercy seat downward
opt4: Hammered of pure silver with faces turned toward the eastern veil
correct: Two cherubims of image work, and overlaid them with gold ... and their faces were inward

And they stood on their feet, and their faces were inward."

question: What was the total combined wingspan of the two golden cherubim spanning the entire width of the Most Holy Place?
opt1: Thirty cubits long, with each wing extending seven and a half cubits

explanation: Each of the four cherub wings measured 5 cubits, creating an unbroken 20-cubit canopy touching both opposite walls of the Holy of Holies and meeting in the center. 2 Chronicles 3:11-13 (KJV) - "And the wings of the cherubims were twenty cubits long: one wing of the one cherub was five cubits, reaching to the wall of the house: and the other wing was likewise five cubits, reaching to the wing of the other cherub ..."

question: What colors and embroidery adorned the sacred inner veil that separated the Holy Place from the Most Holy Place?
opt1: White fine-twined linen embroidered with golden pomegranates and palms
opt2: Scarlet and azure silk interwoven with figures of the sun and moon
opt3: He made the vail of blue, and purple, and crimson, and fine linen, and wrought cherubims thereon
opt4: Deep violet wool overlaid with golden chains and almond blossoms
correct: He made the vail of blue, and purple, and crimson, and fine linen, and wrought cherubims thereon
explanation: Echoing the wilderness tabernacle curtain, Solomon's inner veil was woven of blue, purple, crimson, and fine linen, embroidered with cherubim motifs. 2 Chronicles 3:14 (KJV) - "And he made the vail of blue, and purple, and crimson, and fine linen, and wrought cherubims thereon."

question: What were the names and heights of the two monumental brass pillars erected before the entrance of the temple?
opt1: Two pillars of eighteen cubits high, named Mercy on the right and Truth on the left
opt2: Two pillars of forty cubits high, named Zion on the right and Moriah on the left
opt3: Two pillars of twenty-five cubits high, named Strength on the right and Glory on the left
opt4: He made before the house two pillars of thirty and five cubits high ... and called the name of that on the right hand Jachin, and the name of that on the left Boaz
correct: He made before the house two pillars of thirty and five cubits high ... and called the name of that on the right hand Jachin, and the name of that on the left Boaz
explanation: The two bronze monoliths stood 35 cubits high (with 5-cubit chapiters atop) and were named Jachin ('He will establish') on the south and Boaz ('In Him is strength') on the north. 2 Chronicles 3:15, 17 (KJV) - "Also he made before the house two pillars of thirty and five cubits high, and the chapiter that was on the top of each of them was five cubits ... And he reared up the pillars before the temple, one on the right hand, and the other on the left; and called the name of that on the right hand Jachin, and the name of that on the left Boaz."

question: What were the dimensions of the great brazen altar constructed by Solomon for the temple court?
opt1: Ten cubits square, and five cubits high

opt4: Twenty cubits the length thereof, and twenty cubits the breadth thereof, and ten cubits the height thereof
correct: Twenty cubits the length thereof, and twenty cubits the breadth thereof, and ten cubits the height thereof

question: What were the physical measurements and decorative brim of the colossal bronze Molten Sea?

question: What primary corrupting influence caused King Jehoram to walk in the abominations of the northern kingdom of Israel?

opt2: He walked in the way of the kings of Israel, like as did the house of Ahab: for he had the daughter of Ahab to wife: and he wrought that which was evil in the eyes of the LORD
opt3: He was deceived by the false prophets of Bethel who promised him the wealth of Phoenicia
opt4: He was coerced by the chariot commanders of Egypt who threatened to invade Jerusalem
correct: He walked in the way of the kings of Israel, like as did the house of Ahab: for he had the daughter of Ahab to wife: and he wrought that which was evil in the eyes of the LORD
explanation: Jehoram's apostasy was fueled by his marriage to Athaliah, the daughter of Ahab and Jezebel, introducing Omride pagan corruption into the royal house of Judah. 2 Chronicles 21:6 (KJV) - "And he walked in the way of the kings of Israel, like as did the house of Ahab: for he had the daughter of Ahab to wife: and he wrought that which was evil in the eyes of the LORD."

question: Why did the LORD refrain from destroying the royal house of Judah despite Jehoram's grotesque iniquity?
opt1: Because King Jehoshaphat had offered thousands of sacrifices before his death
opt2: Because the high priest wept before the ark of the covenant on Mount Zion
opt3: Howbeit the LORD would not destroy the house of David, because of the covenant that he had made with David, and as he promised to give a light to him and to his sons for ever
opt4: Because Jehoram paid thirty talents of gold to repair the temple gates
correct: Howbeit the LORD would not destroy the house of David, because of the covenant that he had made with David, and as he promised to give a light to him and to his sons for ever
explanation: Divine covenant faithfulness alone preserved Judah: Yahweh remembered His eternal covenant with David to preserve a perpetual dynastic 'light' (ner) for his lineage. 2 Chronicles 21:7 (KJV) - "Howbeit the LORD would not destroy the house of David, because of the covenant that he had made with David, and as he promised to give a light to him and to his sons for ever."

question: Which two subject nations successfully revolted against Jehoram's imperial rule, fulfilling ancient prophecies?
opt1: The Moabites and the Ammonites revolted and captured the cities of Gilead
opt2: The Philistines of Gaza and the kings of Syria revolted and sacked Joppa
opt3: The Arabians of the desert and the princes of Midian seized Ezion-geber
opt4: In his days the Edomites revolted from under the dominion of Judah, and made themselves a king ... the same time also did Libnah revolt from under his hand; because he had forsaken the LORD God of his fathers
correct: In his days the Edomites revolted from under the dominion of Judah, and made themselves a king ... the same time also did Libnah revolt from under his hand; because he had forsaken the LORD God of his fathers
explanation: Edom threw off the Judean yoke (fulfilling Isaac's prophecy in Gen 27:40), and the priestly fortress city of Libnah revolted because Jehoram had apostatized from Yahweh. 2 Chronicles 21:8, 10 (KJV) - "In his days the Edomites revolted from under the dominion of Judah, and made themselves a king ... The same time also did Libnah revolt from under his hand; because he had forsaken the LORD God of his fathers."

question: What unique written prophetic communication was delivered to King Jehoram, and who authored it?
opt1: And there came a writing to him from Elijah the prophet
opt2: And there came a scroll to him from Elisha the prophet at Dothan
opt3: And there came a letter to him from Micaiah the prophet from the prison house
opt4: And there came an oracle to him from Jehu the seer from the high place of Ramah
correct: And there came a writing to him from Elijah the prophet
explanation: In an extraordinary and sole recorded instance in Chronicles, a posthumous or dispatched written missive ('a writing') from the northern prophet Elijah was delivered directly to Jehoram. 2 Chronicles 21:12 (KJV) - "And there came a writing to him from Elijah the prophet, saying, Thus saith the LORD God of David thy father ..."

question: What severe moral crimes did Elijah's written oracle charge against King Jehoram?
opt1: 'Because thou hast sold the temple vessels to the merchants of Tyre and neglected the Sabbath'
opt2: 'Because thou hast not walked in the ways of Jehoshaphat thy father ... but hast walked in the way of the kings of Israel, and hast made Judah and the inhabitants of Jerusalem to go a whoring, like to the whoredoms of the house of Ahab, and also hast slain thy brethren of thy father's house, which were better than thyself'
opt3: 'Because thou didst flee from the battlefield of Ramoth-gilead and refused to bury Ahab'
opt4: 'Because thou hast formed an alliance with the king of Babylon and sacrificed thine own sons'
correct: 'Because thou hast not walked in the ways of Jehoshaphat thy father ... but hast walked in the way of the kings of Israel, and hast made Judah and the inhabitants of Jerusalem to go a whoring, like to the whoredoms of the house of Ahab, and also hast slain thy brethren of thy father's house, which were better than thyself'
explanation: Elijah's letter indicted Jehoram for apostatizing into Ahab's spiritual harlotry and executing his innocent brothers, who were morally superior to himself. 2 Chronicles 21:12-13 (KJV) - "... Because thou hast not walked in the ways of Jehoshaphat thy father, nor in the ways of Asa king of Judah, But hast walked in the way of the kings of Israel, and hast made Judah and the inhabitants of Jerusalem to go a whoring, like to the whoredoms of the house of Ahab, and also hast slain thy brethren of thy father's house, which were better than thyself ..."

question: What horrific physical plague and disease did Elijah's letter predict would strike Jehoram personally?
opt1: 'Thou shalt be smitten with incurable leprosy from the crown of thy head unto thy feet'
opt2: 'A consuming fire shall scorch thy flesh until thy bones crumble into white ash'
opt3: 'And thou shalt have great sickness by disease of thy bowels, until thy bowels fall out by reason of the sickness day by day'
opt4: 'Thou shalt be struck with perpetual blindness and madness of heart before thy people'
correct: 'And thou shalt have great sickness by disease of thy bowels, until thy bowels fall out by reason of the sickness day by day'
explanation: Elijah prophesied a protracted, excruciating, and fatal gastrointestinal affliction whereby Jehoram's bowels would literally prolapse and discharge over time. 2 Chronicles 21:15 (KJV) - "And thou shalt have great sickness by disease of thy bowels, until thy bowels fall out by reason of the sickness day by day."

question: Which hostile nations did the LORD stir up to sack Jerusalem and plunder Jehoram's royal household?
opt1: The armies of Syria and the chariot forces of Moab invaded and leveled the citadel
opt2: The king of Assyria and the princes of Ammon plundered the gold of the temple
opt3: The kingdom of Egypt and the mercenaries of Midian took all the cattle of Judah
opt4: The LORD stirred up against Jehoram the spirit of the Philistines, and of the Arabians, that were near the Ethiopians: And they came up into Judah, and brake into it, and carried away all the substance that was found in the king's house, and his sons also, and his wives
correct: The LORD stirred up against Jehoram the spirit of the Philistines, and of the Arabians, that were near the Ethiopians: And they came up into Judah, and brake into it, and carried away all the substance that was found in the king's house, and his sons also, and his wives
explanation: Yahweh stirred up Philistine and coastal Arabian raiders, who breached Jerusalem, looted the royal palace, and captured all of Jehoram's wives and sons except the youngest. 2 Chronicles 21:16-17 (KJV) - "Moreover the LORD stirred up against Jehoram the spirit of the Philistines, and of the Arabians, that were near the Ethiopians: And they came up into Judah, and brake into it, and carried away all the substance that was found in the king's house, and his sons also, and his wives; so that there was never a son left him, save Jehoahaz, the youngest of his sons."

question: Which of King Jehoram's sons alone survived this foreign invasion and plunder?
opt1: Jehoahaz, the youngest of his sons (also called Ahaziah)
opt2: Joash, the infant son hidden by the high priest
opt3: Amaziah, the eldest son born of the princess of Tyre
opt4: Zechariah, the prophet's son who dwelt in the temple
correct: Jehoahaz, the youngest of his sons (also called Ahaziah)
explanation: Only his youngest son, Jehoahaz (designated Ahaziah in subsequent chapters), survived the devastating raid. 2 Chronicles 21:17 (KJV) - "... so that there was never a son left him, save Jehoahaz, the youngest of his sons."

question: What ignominious details marked the agonizing death, funeral, and burial of King Jehoram in 2 Chronicles 21:19-20?
opt1: He was murdered by his eunuchs in his bedchamber and cast into the brook Kidron
opt2: His bowels fell out by reason of his sickness: so he died of sore diseases. And his people made no burning for him, like the burning of his fathers ... and departed without being desired. Howbeit they buried him in the city of David, but not in the sepulchres of the kings
opt3: He died of leprosy in an isolated house and was buried in the potter's field without tears
opt4: He died during a siege of Jerusalem and was thrown over the wall to the invading Arabians
correct: His bowels fell out by reason of his sickness: so he died of sore diseases. And his people made no burning for him, like the burning of his fathers ... and departed without being desired. Howbeit they buried him in the city of David, but not in the sepulchres of the kings
explanation: Jehoram suffered a two-year agonizing death, received no royal aromatic burning, died unmourned and unregretted ('departed without being desired'), and was denied burial in the sacred tombs of the Davidic kings. 2 Chronicles 21:19-20 (KJV) - "And it came to pass, that in process of time, after the end of two years, his bowels fell out by reason of his sickness: so he died of sore diseases. And his people made no burning for him, like the burning of his fathers. Thirty and two years old was he when he began to reign, and he reigned in Jerusalem eight years, and departed without being desired. Howbeit they buried him in the city of David, but not in the sepulchres of the kings."

question: Why did the citizens of Jerusalem make Ahaziah, the youngest son of Jehoram, king in his stead?
opt1: Because Jehoram had chosen him before his death in the presence of the high priest
opt2: For the band of men that came with the Arabians to the camp had slain all the eldest. So Ahaziah the son of Jehoram king of Judah reigned
opt3: Because the elders of Judah cast sacred lots upon Mount Zion and the lot fell on Ahaziah
opt4: Because his older brothers had contracted Jehoram's fatal bowel disease and died in Samaria
correct: For the band of men that came with the Arabians to the camp had slain all the eldest. So Ahaziah the son of Jehoram king of Judah reigned
explanation: Ahaziah alone among Jehoram's sons survived because Arabian desert raiders had slaughtered all his older brothers during their raid on Jerusalem. 2 Chronicles 22:1 (KJV) - "And the inhabitants of Jerusalem made Ahaziah his youngest son king in his stead: for the band of men that came with the Arabians to the camp had slain all the eldest. So Ahaziah the son of Jehoram king of Judah reigned."

question: Who was Ahaziah's mother, and what destructive moral influence did she and her northern family exercise over his reign?
opt1: His mother was Maachah of Tyre, who hired Syrian mercenaries to enforce pagan worship
opt2: His mother was Zibiah of Beersheba, who advised him to empty the temple treasuries for Egypt
opt3: His mother's name also was Athaliah the daughter of Omri. He also walked in the ways of the house of Ahab: for his mother was his counsellor to do wickedly ... for they were his counsellors after the death of his father to his destruction
opt4: His mother was Jehoaddan of Samaria, who established the worship of Chemosh on Mount Moriah
correct: His mother's name also was Athaliah the daughter of Omri. He also walked in the ways of the house of Ahab: for his mother was his counsellor to do wickedly ... for they were his counsellors after the death of his father to his destruction
explanation: Athaliah, daughter/granddaughter of Omri and daughter of Ahab, served as Ahaziah's wicked counsellor, steering the Davidic court into Omride apostasy and ultimate ruin. 2 Chronicles 22:2-4 (KJV) - "... His mother's name also was Athaliah the daughter of Omri. He also walked in the ways of the house of Ahab: for his mother was his counsellor to do wickedly. Wherefore he did evil in the sight of the LORD like the house of Ahab: for they were his counsellors after the death of his father to his destruction."

question: What theological explanation does 2 Chronicles 22:7 give for Ahaziah's journey to visit wounded King Joram at Jezreel?
opt1: Because Satan provoked Ahaziah to form a covenant with the wounded king of Israel
opt2: Because Hazael king of Syria had threatened to besiege Jerusalem if Ahaziah did not visit Jezreel
opt3: Because the physicians of Judah advised him to seek the medicinal herbs of the valley of Jezreel
opt4: And the destruction of Ahaziah was of God by coming to Joram: for when he was come, he went out with Jehoram against Jehu the son of Nimshi, whom the LORD had anointed to cut off the house of Ahab
correct: And the destruction of Ahaziah was of God by coming to Joram: for when he was come, he went out with Jehoram against Jehu the son of Nimshi, whom the LORD had anointed to cut off the house of Ahab
explanation: The chronicler identifies divine judgment behind Ahaziah's journey: God orchestrated his visit to Jezreel so that he would be caught in Jehu's divinely commissioned purge of Ahab's dynasty. 2 Chronicles 22:7 (KJV) - "And the destruction of Ahaziah was of God by coming to Joram: for when he was come, he went out with Jehoram against Jehu the son of Nimshi, whom the LORD had anointed to cut off the house of Ahab."

question: Whom did Jehu execute when he encountered them ministering to Ahaziah during his judicial purge?
opt1: Jehu executed judgment upon the house of Ahab, and found the princes of Judah, and the sons of the brethren of Ahaziah, that ministered to Ahaziah, he slew them
opt2: He slew forty priests of Baal and the chariot drivers of Samaria
opt3: He executed the foreign ambassadors of Damascus and the tax collectors of Tyre
opt4: He captured fifty Levite singers and sent them in chains to the king of Assyria
correct: Jehu executed judgment upon the house of Ahab, and found the princes of Judah, and the sons of the brethren of Ahaziah, that ministered to Ahaziah, he slew them
explanation: Executing Yahweh's wrath upon Omride corruption, Jehu intercepted and executed 42 royal princes of Judah who were allied with Ahaziah. 2 Chronicles 22:8 (KJV) - "And it came to pass, that, when Jehu was executing judgment upon the house of Ahab, and found the princes of Judah, and the sons of the brethren of Ahaziah, that ministered to Ahaziah, he slew them."

question: Where was Ahaziah discovered hiding, and why was he granted an honorable royal burial after Jehu executed him?
opt1: He was hid in a cave at Megiddo, and was buried because he had built the walls of Beth-shemesh
opt2: He sought Ahaziah: and they caught him, (for he was hid in Samaria,) and brought him to Jehu: and when they had slain him, they buried him: Because, said they, he is the son of Jehoshaphat, who sought the LORD with all his heart
opt3: He was hid in a well at Jezreel, and was buried because he was of the royal seed of Solomon
opt4: He was hid in the temple of Baal, and was buried because the elders of Samaria wept for him
correct: He sought Ahaziah: and they caught him, (for he was hid in Samaria,) and brought him to Jehu: and when they had slain him, they buried him: Because, said they, he is the son of Jehoshaphat, who sought the LORD with all his heart
explanation: Captured in Samaria and put to death by Jehu, Ahaziah was granted burial solely out of lingering respect for the righteous legacy of his grandfather Jehoshaphat. 2 Chronicles 22:9 (KJV) - "And he sought Ahaziah: and they caught him, (for he was hid in Samaria,) and brought him to Jehu: and when they had slain him, they buried him: Because, said they, he is the son of Jehoshaphat, who sought the LORD with all his heart. So the house of Ahaziah had no power to keep still the kingdom."

question: What bloodthirsty coup did Queen Mother Athaliah execute upon learning that her son Ahaziah was dead?
opt1: She surrendered Jerusalem to the king of Syria and retired to the palace of Samaria
opt2: She proclaimed her grandson king and appointed twelve Baalite elders as regents
opt3: When Athaliah the mother of Ahaziah saw that her son was dead, she arose and destroyed all the seed royal of the house of Judah
opt4: She fled to Tyre with the golden shields and melted them for foreign mercenaries
correct: When Athaliah the mother of Ahaziah saw that her son was dead, she arose and destroyed all the seed royal of the house of Judah
explanation: Seeking total tyrannical power and the eradication of David's line, ruthless Athaliah systematically slaughtered her own grandsons—all royal claimants of the Davidic dynasty. 2 Chronicles 22:10 (KJV) - "But when Athaliah the mother of Ahaziah saw that her son was dead, she arose and destroyed all the seed royal of the house of Judah."

question: Who heroically rescued the infant prince Joash from Athaliah's royal massacre, and what was her relation to the royal family and priesthood?
opt1: Zibiah of Beersheba, the nurse of the royal nursery and cousin of the high priest
opt2: Jehoaddan of Jerusalem, the queen consort and daughter of Zadok the priest
opt3: Jerushah the prophetess, the widow of King Asa and aunt of Ahaziah
opt4: Jehoshabeath, the daughter of the king, took Joash the son of Ahaziah, and stole him from among the king's sons that were slain ... (for she was the daughter of king Jehoram, the wife of Jehoiada the priest, for she was the sister of Ahaziah)
correct: Jehoshabeath, the daughter of the king, took Joash the son of Ahaziah, and stole him from among the king's sons that were slain ... (for she was the daughter of king Jehoram, the wife of Jehoiada the priest, for she was the sister of Ahaziah)
explanation: Princess Jehoshabeath (Jehosheba), daughter of Jehoram, sister of Ahaziah, and wife of High Priest Jehoiada, courageously preserved the Messianic seed line by smuggling baby Joash out of the slaughter. 2 Chronicles 22:11 (KJV) - "But Jehoshabeath, the daughter of the king, took Joash the son of Ahaziah, and stole him from among the king's sons that were slain, and put him and his nurse in a bedchamber. So Jehoshabeath, the daughter of king Jehoram, the wife of Jehoiada the priest, (for she was the sister of Ahaziah,) hid him from Athaliah, so that she slew him not."

question: Where was the infant Joash hidden from Athaliah, and for how many years did the usurping queen rule the land?
opt1: And he was with them hid in the house of God six years: and Athaliah reigned over the land
opt2: Hid in a subterranean chamber beneath the city of David for seven years
opt3: Hid in the fortress of Lachish under the care of Levite guards for three years
opt4: Hid in the wilderness of En-gedi in the caves of David for five years
correct: And he was with them hid in the house of God six years: and Athaliah reigned over the land
explanation: The child prince was covertly raised in the temple residential chambers for six years while Athaliah exercised tyrannical rule over Judah. 2 Chronicles 22:12 (KJV) - "And he was with them hid in the house of God six years: and Athaliah reigned over the land."

question: What immediate domestic location did Jehoshabeath use to conceal infant Joash and his nurse during the massacre?
opt1: Concealed him beneath the brazen sea among the twelve bronze oxen
opt2: Put him and his nurse in a bedchamber ... hid him from Athaliah, so that she slew him not
opt3: Hid him inside the golden cedar chest of dedicated spoils in the oracle
opt4: Placed him in a linen basket and lowered him down the wall of Ophel
correct: Put him and his nurse in a bedchamber ... hid him from Athaliah, so that she slew him not
explanation: She initially concealed Joash and his wet nurse in a temple palace storage bedchamber before transferring him into permanent sanctuary quarters. 2 Chronicles 22:11 (KJV) - "... and put him and his nurse in a bedchamber. So Jehoshabeath ... hid him from Athaliah, so that she slew him not."

question: What genealogical distinction made Jehoshabeath uniquely situated to bridge the royal palace and the sacred temple?
opt1: She was the daughter of the high priest of Bethel and married to the chief captain of Judah
opt2: She was an adopted princess of Egypt married to the royal recorder of Jerusalem
opt3: She was of royal Davidic blood as daughter of King Jehoram and sister of King Ahaziah, while simultaneously married to Jehoiada the high priest of Yahweh
opt4: She was a descendant of Nathan the prophet married to the commander of the temple guard
correct: She was of royal Davidic blood as daughter of King Jehoram and sister of King Ahaziah, while simultaneously married to Jehoiada the high priest of Yahweh
explanation: Her marriage united the Davidic monarchy with the Aaronite high priesthood, enabling sanctuary asylum and political legitimacy for the hidden heir. 2 Chronicles 22:11 (KJV) - "... So Jehoshabeath, the daughter of king Jehoram, the wife of Jehoiada the priest, (for she was the sister of Ahaziah,) hid him from Athaliah, so that she slew him not."

question: In which year did High Priest Jehoiada initiate the counter-revolution to crown Joash, and with whom did he forge a solemn military covenant?
opt1: In the fifth year, taking the seventy elders of Jerusalem and the priests of Aaron into covenant
opt2: In the twelfth year, taking the commanders of the chariot divisions of Benjamin into covenant
opt3: In the seventh year Jehoiada strengthened himself, and took the captains of hundreds, Azariah the son of Jeroham, and Ishmael the son of Jehohanan, and Azariah the son of Obed, and Maaseiah the son of Adaiah, and Elishaphat the son of Zichri, into covenant with him
opt4: In the third year, taking the Levite singers and the gatekeepers of the temple into covenant
correct: In the seventh year Jehoiada strengthened himself, and took the captains of hundreds, Azariah the son of Jeroham, and Ishmael the son of Jehohanan, and Azariah the son of Obed, and Maaseiah the son of Adaiah, and Elishaphat the son of Zichri, into covenant with him
explanation: In Athaliah's 7th year, Jehoiada secretly enlisted five trusted military commanders of hundreds into a solemn covenant to restore the Davidic monarchy. 2 Chronicles 23:1 (KJV) - "And in the seventh year Jehoiada strengthened himself, and took the captains of hundreds, Azariah the son of Jeroham, and Ishmael the son of Jehohanan, and Azariah the son of Obed, and Maaseiah the son of Adaiah, and Elishaphat the son of Zichri, into covenant with him."

question: What fundamental theological and dynastic promise did Jehoiada declare to the assembled congregation in the house of God?
opt1: 'The priesthood of Aaron shall govern Judah until the temple of Baal is pulverized'
opt2: 'The nation shall cast sacred lots before the ark to choose a king from the house of Jesse'
opt3: 'The sword of Phinehas shall execute Athaliah and the crown shall return to Ephraim'
opt4: 'Behold, the king's son shall reign, as the LORD hath said of the sons of David'
correct: 'Behold, the king's son shall reign, as the LORD hath said of the sons of David'
explanation: Jehoiada anchored the counter-coup in the inviolable Davidic Covenant, asserting that a son of David must reign according to Yahweh's immutable promise. 2 Chronicles 23:3 (KJV) - "And all the congregation made a covenant with the king in the house of God. And he said unto them, Behold, the king's son shall reign, as the LORD hath said of the sons of David."

question: What strict sanctuary holiness regulation did Jehoiada enforce regarding entry into the temple building during the coronation?
opt1: 'None shall come into the house of the LORD, save the priests, and they that minister of the Levites; they shall go in, for they are holy: but all the people shall keep the watch of the LORD'

opt4: 'No man may enter the temple except the seven-year-old king and his royal nurse'
correct: 'None shall come into the house of the LORD, save the priests, and they that minister of the Levites; they shall go in, for they are holy: but all the people shall keep the watch of the LORD'
explanation: Even during an armed revolution, Jehoiada scrupulously upheld Mosaic holiness: only consecrated priests and Levites were permitted inside the sanctuary edifice. 2 Chronicles 23:6 (KJV) - "But let none come into the house of the LORD, save the priests, and they that minister of the Levites; they shall go in, for they are holy: but all the people shall keep the watch of the LORD."

question: What historic weapons did Jehoiada distribute from the temple armory to the captains of hundreds?
opt1: The bronze weapons taken from the Ethiopians by King Asa in the valley of Zephathah
opt2: Jehoiada the priest delivered to the captains of hundreds spears, and bucklers, and shields, that had been king David's, which were in the house of God
opt3: The three hundred golden shields forged by Solomon for the forest of Lebanon
opt4: The iron broadswords and armor plundered from the Syrians at Ramoth-gilead
correct: Jehoiada the priest delivered to the captains of hundreds spears, and bucklers, and shields, that had been king David's, which were in the house of God
explanation: Jehoiada armed the officers with the consecrated spears, bucklers, and shields originally dedicated by King David and preserved in the temple armory. 2 Chronicles 23:9 (KJV) - "Moreover Jehoiada the priest delivered to the captains of hundreds spears, and bucklers, and shields, that had been king David's, which were in the house of God."

question: What three sacred coronation acts were performed when young Joash was presented to the nation in the temple court?
opt1: They washed his feet in the molten sea, put on him the linen ephod, and blew the silver shofars
opt2: They girded him with David's sword, seated him upon the brazen scaffold, and offered twenty bullocks
opt3: Then they brought out the king's son, and put upon him the crown, and gave him the testimony, and made him king. And Jehoiada and his sons anointed him, and said, God save the king
opt4: They gave him the golden sceptre of Solomon, placed him before the cherubim, and cast incense

explanation: The coronation followed ancient royal theocratic liturgy: crowning him, placing the scroll of the Law ('the testimony') in his hands, anointing him, and acclaming 'God save the king'. 2 Chronicles 23:11 (KJV) - "Then they brought out the king's son, and put upon him the crown, and gave him the testimony, and made him king. And Jehoiada and his sons anointed him, and said, God save the king."

question: What sight greeted Queen Athaliah when she rushed into the temple court upon hearing the tumult of the shouting populace?

correct: She looked, and, behold, the king stood at his pillar at the entering in, and the princes and the trumpets by the king: and all the people of the land rejoiced, and sounded with trumpets, also the singers with instruments of musick, and such as taught to sing praise. Then Athaliah rent her clothes, and said, Treason, Treason
explanation: Athaliah witnessed the seven-year-old crowned king standing by the royal entrance pillar surrounded by jubilant citizens, trumpeters, and musicians; rending her garments, she screamed 'Treason! Treason!'. 2 Chronicles 23:13 (KJV) - "She looked, and, behold, the king stood at his pillar at the entering in, and the princes and the trumpets by the king: and all the people of the land rejoiced, and sounded with trumpets, also the singers with instruments of musick, and such as taught to sing praise. Then Athaliah rent her clothes, and said, Treason, Treason."

question: Where did Jehoiada command that Athaliah be executed, and why was she not slain inside the temple court?
