opt2: In the valley of Hinnom; because the blood of a queen could not be shed near Mount Moriah
opt3: At the water gate by the brook Kidron; because the law forbade executing women in holy places
opt4: In the prison of the court of the guard; because she was condemned to die by starvation
correct: Have her forth of the ranges ... Slay her not in the house of the LORD. So they laid hands on her; and when she was come to the entering of the horse gate by the king's house, they slew her there
explanation: Jehoiada prohibited desecrating the temple court with her execution, commanding officers to escort her past the ranks and execute her outside at the palace Horse Gate. 2 Chronicles 23:14-15 (KJV) - "Then Jehoiada the priest brought out the captains of hundreds ... and said unto them, Have her forth of the ranges ... For the priest said, Slay her not in the house of the LORD. So they laid hands on her; and when she was come to the entering of the horse gate by the king's house, they slew her there."

question: What tri-partite covenant was ratified by Jehoiada immediately following Athaliah's execution?
opt1: A covenant between Judah, Benjamin, and the priests to rebuild the walls of Jerusalem
opt2: Jehoiada made a covenant between him, and between all the people, and between the king, that they should be the LORD's people
opt3: A military pact between the army captains and the royal house to conquer the Philistines
opt4: A trade treaty between the merchants of Jerusalem and the Phoenician sea captains
correct: Jehoiada made a covenant between him, and between all the people, and between the king, that they should be the LORD's people
explanation: Jehoiada brokered a comprehensive renewal of the national covenant uniting priest, people, and monarch in mutual pledge to be Yahweh's holy people. 2 Chronicles 23:16 (KJV) - "And Jehoiada made a covenant between him, and between all the people, and between the king, that they should be the LORD's people."

question: What anti-idolatry purge did the people of Judah execute immediately after renewing the covenant?
opt1: They burned all foreign merchant ships anchored at the port of Joppa
opt2: They pulverized the golden calf shrines of Bethel and cast the dust into the Jordan
opt3: All the people went to the house of Baal, and brake it down, and brake his altars and his images in pieces, and slew Mattan the priest of Baal before the altars
opt4: They banished all Ammonite and Moabite resident aliens from the cities of Judah
correct: All the people went to the house of Baal, and brake it down, and brake his altars and his images in pieces, and slew Mattan the priest of Baal before the altars
explanation: The newly reformed populace demolished the temple of Baal established during Athaliah's reign, pulverizing its altars and images and executing Mattan, the chief Baalite priest. 2 Chronicles 23:17 (KJV) - "Then all the people went to the house of Baal, and brake it down, and brake his altars and his images in pieces, and slew Mattan the priest of Baal before the altars."

question: How did the coronation proceedings conclude in 2 Chronicles 23:20-21 as Joash was escorted into the palace?
opt1: They carried the king upon a golden chariot through the valley of Kidron, and fasted for three days
opt2: They blew one hundred and twenty silver trumpets on Mount Zion, and the Philistines sued for peace
opt3: They offered ten thousand sheep in the middle court, and the elders of Samaria paid royal homage
opt4: They brought down the king from the house of the LORD ... through the high gate into the king's house, and set the king upon the throne of the kingdom. And all the people of the land rejoiced: and the city was quiet, after that they had slain Athaliah with the sword
correct: They brought down the king from the house of the LORD ... through the high gate into the king's house, and set the king upon the throne of the kingdom. And all the people of the land rejoiced: and the city was quiet, after that they had slain Athaliah with the sword
explanation: Young Joash was escorted through the High Gate and seated upon the royal throne of David; Athaliah's usurpation ended, the city was quiet, and national joy was restored. 2 Chronicles 23:20-21 (KJV) - "And he took the captains of hundreds ... and brought down the king from the house of the LORD: and they came through the high gate into the king's house, and set the king upon the throne of the kingdom. And all the people of the land rejoiced: and the city was quiet, after that they had slain Athaliah with the sword."

question: How old was Joash when he ascended the throne of Judah, and what spiritual qualification governed his early reign?
opt1: He was twelve years old and reigned twenty-five years; and he walked in all the ways of Solomon
opt2: He was sixteen years old and reigned fifty years; and he built the high gate of the temple
opt3: He was ten years old and reigned thirty-three years; and he was guided by Nathan the prophet
opt4: Joash was seven years old when he began to reign, and he reigned forty years in Jerusalem ... And Joash did that which was right in the sight of the LORD all the days of Jehoiada the priest
correct: Joash was seven years old when he began to reign, and he reigned forty years in Jerusalem ... And Joash did that which was right in the sight of the LORD all the days of Jehoiada the priest
explanation: Joash was crowned at age seven, reigning forty years; his righteous behavior, however, was fundamentally dependent upon the spiritual mentorship of High Priest Jehoiada. 2 Chronicles 24:1-2 (KJV) - "Joash was seven years old when he began to reign, and he reigned forty years in Jerusalem. His mother's name also was Zibiah of Beer-sheba. And Joash did that which was right in the sight of the LORD all the days of Jehoiada the priest."

question: What major architectural and religious initiative did King Joash determine to undertake, and what complaint did he bring against the Levites?
opt1: Joash was minded to repair the house of the LORD ... and said to the Levites, Go out unto the cities of Judah, and gather of all Israel money to repair the house of your God from year to year, and see that ye hasten the matter. Howbeit the Levites hastened it not
opt2: He determined to rebuild the walls of Jerusalem, but the Levites refused to quarry stone
opt3: He sought to forge new bronze pillars, but the priests kept the copper for their own households
opt4: He planned to construct a new royal palace, but the Levites demanded higher tithes
correct: Joash was minded to repair the house of the LORD ... and said to the Levites, Go out unto the cities of Judah, and gather of all Israel money to repair the house of your God from year to year, and see that ye hasten the matter. Howbeit the Levites hastened it not
explanation: Joash resolved to restore the dilapidated temple, commanding Levites to collect the annual national repair tax; however, the Levites delayed and neglected the administrative work. 2 Chronicles 24:4-5 (KJV) - "And it came to pass after this, that Joash was minded to repair the house of the LORD. And he gathered together the priests and the Levites, and said to them, Go out unto the cities of Judah, and gather of all Israel money to repair the house of your God from year to year, and see that ye hasten the matter. Howbeit the Levites hastened it not."

question: What historical sacrilege had been committed against the house of God by the family of Athaliah, as cited in 2 Chronicles 24:7?
opt1: They had burned the cedar ceiling of the oracle and stolen the two tables of stone
opt2: For the sons of Athaliah, that wicked woman, had broken up the house of God; and also all the dedicated things of the house of the LORD did they bestow upon Baalim
opt3: They had melted the golden menorahs to pay tribute to the king of Assyria
opt4: They had converted the inner court into a chariot stable for Phoenician cavalry
correct: For the sons of Athaliah, that wicked woman, had broken up the house of God; and also all the dedicated things of the house of the LORD did they bestow upon Baalim
explanation: Athaliah's sons had systematically vandalized the sanctuary, plundering consecrated temple furnishings and dedicating sacred Yahwistic treasures to the worship of the Baals. 2 Chronicles 24:7 (KJV) - "For the sons of Athaliah, that wicked woman, had broken up the house of God; and also all the dedicated things of the house of the LORD did they bestow upon Baalim."

question: What innovative financial collection mechanism did King Joash command to be fabricated and placed at the temple gate?
opt1: They placed twelve bronze basins in the court of the priests to receive silver coins
opt2: They established a royal counting house in the high gate under five Levite scribes
opt3: At the king's commandment they made a chest, and set it without at the gate of the house of the LORD. And they made a proclamation through Judah and Jerusalem, to bring in to the LORD the collection that Moses the servant of God laid upon Israel in the wilderness
opt4: They erected a stone pillar with an iron funnel beside the brazen altar for gold dust
correct: At the king's commandment they made a chest, and set it without at the gate of the house of the LORD. And they made a proclamation through Judah and Jerusalem, to bring in to the LORD the collection that Moses the servant of God laid upon Israel in the wilderness
explanation: Bypassing clerical inertia, Joash instituted the famed 'Jehoiada chest' system: a locked collection chest outside the temple gate where citizens deposited the Mosaic wilderness tabernacle poll tax directly. 2 Chronicles 24:8-9 (KJV) - "And at the king's commandment they made a chest, and set it without at the gate of the house of the LORD. And they made a proclamation through Judah and Jerusalem, to bring in to the LORD the collection that Moses the servant of God laid upon Israel in the wilderness."

question: How did the princes and the general public respond to this new collection chest system?
opt1: They murmured against the king and refused to contribute silver for three months
opt2: They demanded that the high priest provide receipts stamped with the royal signet
opt3: Only the wealthy elders of Jerusalem contributed, while provincial citizens withheld funds
opt4: And all the princes and all the people rejoiced, and brought in, and cast into the chest, until they had made an end
correct: And all the princes and all the people rejoiced, and brought in, and cast into the chest, until they had made an end
explanation: The populace responded with exuberant generosity, joyfully filling the collection chest with abundant funds until the repair goal was achieved. 2 Chronicles 24:10 (KJV) - "And all the princes and all the people rejoiced, and brought in, and cast into the chest, until they had made an end."

question: At what exceptional age did High Priest Jehoiada die, and where was he buried in recognition of his monumental national service?
opt1: Jehoiada waxed old, and was full of days when he died; an hundred and thirty years old was he when he died. And they buried him in the city of David among the kings, because he had done good in Israel, both toward God, and toward his house
opt2: He died at age ninety-five and was buried in the cave of Machpelah with Abraham
opt3: He died at age one hundred and ten and was buried in the ancestral tomb of Aaron at Mount Hor
opt4: He died at age one hundred and twenty and was buried in the court of the priests beside the altar
correct: Jehoiada waxed old, and was full of days when he died; an hundred and thirty years old was he when he died. And they buried him in the city of David among the kings, because he had done good in Israel, both toward God, and toward his house
explanation: Jehoiada died at the patriarchal age of 130 and was accorded the supreme national honor of burial among the Davidic kings in the City of David for his heroic spiritual and civil service. 2 Chronicles 24:15-16 (KJV) - "But Jehoiada waxed old, and was full of days when he died; an hundred and thirty years old was he when he died. And they buried him in the city of David among the kings, because he had done good in Israel, both toward God, and toward his house."

question: What disastrous spiritual collapse unfolded in Judah immediately following Jehoiada's death in 2 Chronicles 24:17-18?
opt1: The priests of Aaron revolted and demanded that Joash surrender his crown to Jehoiada's son
opt2: Now after the death of Jehoiada came the princes of Judah, and made obeisance to the king. Then the king hearkened unto them. And they left the house of the LORD God of their fathers, and served groves and idols: and wrath came upon Judah and Jerusalem for this their trespass
opt3: The king of Egypt invaded Jerusalem and burned the newly repaired cedar doors of the temple
opt4: The Levites ceased offering burnt offerings and fled into the mountains of Ephraim
correct: Now after the death of Jehoiada came the princes of Judah, and made obeisance to the king. Then the king hearkened unto them. And they left the house of the LORD God of their fathers, and served groves and idols: and wrath came upon Judah and Jerusalem for this their trespass
explanation: Lacking deep personal spiritual convictions, Joash succumbed to the flattery of apostate Judean nobles, abandoning Yahweh's temple to worship Asherah groves and pagan idols. 2 Chronicles 24:17-18 (KJV) - "Now after the death of Jehoiada came the princes of Judah, and made obeisance to the king. Then the king hearkened unto them. And they left the house of the LORD God of their fathers, and served groves and idols: and wrath came upon Judah and Jerusalem for this their trespass."

question: Which prophetic priest was empowered by the Spirit of God to rebuke the backslidden court, and what martyrdom did King Joash command against him?
opt1: The prophet Azariah: Joash cast him into a pit of mire beneath the gate of Benjamin
opt2: The prophet Hanani: Joash put him in the stocks of the prison house until he perished
opt3: The Spirit of God came upon Zechariah the son of Jehoiada the priest ... And they conspired against him, and stoned him with stones at the commandment of the king in the court of the house of the LORD
opt4: The prophet Micaiah: Joash fed him with bread of affliction in the fortress of Lachish
correct: The Spirit of God came upon Zechariah the son of Jehoiada the priest ... And they conspired against him, and stoned him with stones at the commandment of the king in the court of the house of the LORD
explanation: Zechariah, son of Joash's benefactor Jehoiada, was filled with the Spirit to confront the apostasy; in horrific betrayal, Joash commanded that Zechariah be stoned to death in the sacred temple court. 2 Chronicles 24:20-21 (KJV) - "And the Spirit of God came upon Zechariah the son of Jehoiada the priest, which stood above the people, and said unto them, Thus saith God, Why transgress ye the commandments of the LORD, that ye cannot prosper? because ye have forsaken the LORD, he hath also forsaken you. And they conspired against him, and stoned him with stones at the commandment of the king in the court of the house of the LORD."

question: What dying prophetic prayer did Zechariah utter as he was being martyred, and how did God avenge his blood through the Syrian army?
opt1: He said, Lay not this sin to their charge; but a plague of boils struck all the princes of Judah
opt2: He said, Let Mount Moriah be cursed; and an earthquake shattered the walls of the palace
opt3: He said, May the throne of David be darkened; and Pharaoh invaded and plundered Jerusalem
opt4: When he died, he said, The LORD look upon it, and require it ... And the army of the Syrians came with a small company of men, and the LORD delivered a very great host into their hand, because they had forsaken the LORD God of their fathers
correct: When he died, he said, The LORD look upon it, and require it ... And the army of the Syrians came with a small company of men, and the LORD delivered a very great host into their hand, because they had forsaken the LORD God of their fathers
explanation: Zechariah's dying plea—'The LORD look upon it, and require it' (echoed by Christ in Matt 23:35)—was swiftly answered when a small Syrian detachment routed Judah's massive host, plundering Jerusalem and slaughtering its princes. 2 Chronicles 24:22, 24 (KJV) - "Thus Joash the king remembered not the kindness which Jehoiada his father had done to him, but slew his son. And when he died, he said, The LORD look upon it, and require it ... For the army of the Syrians came with a small company of men, and the LORD delivered a very great host into their hand, because they had forsaken the LORD God of their fathers. So they executed judgment against Joash."

question: How did King Joash meet his end, and what dishonor attended his burial in 2 Chronicles 24:25?
opt1: His own servants conspired against him for the blood of the sons of Jehoiada the priest, and slew him on his bed, and he died: and they buried him in the city of David, but they buried him not in the sepulchres of the kings
opt2: He was killed by an arrow shot by Hazael of Syria and buried in the valley of Hinnom
opt3: He died of his severe wounds in Beth-millo and was cast into the brook Kidron
opt4: He was poisoned by the priests of Aaron and buried in an unmarked tomb at Bethlehem
correct: His own servants conspired against him for the blood of the sons of Jehoiada the priest, and slew him on his bed, and he died: and they buried him in the city of David, but they buried him not in the sepulchres of the kings
explanation: Bedridden with severe wounds, Joash was assassinated in his bed by his own palace conspirators (Zabad and Jehozabad) to avenge Jehoiada's murdered sons; like Jehoram, he was denied burial in the royal tombs of the kings. 2 Chronicles 24:25 (KJV) - "And when they were departed from him ... his own servants conspired against him for the blood of the sons of Jehoiada the priest, and slew him on his bed, and he died: and they buried him in the city of David, but they buried him not in the sepulchres of the kings."

question: What defining theological evaluation is pronounced upon King Amaziah's character and reign in 2 Chronicles 25:2?
opt1: And he did that which was right in the sight of the LORD, but not with a perfect heart
opt2: And he did evil in the sight of the LORD, walking in all the sins of Jeroboam
opt3: And he was accounted righteous like unto David his father all the days of his life
opt4: And his heart was lifted up with pride from the beginning of his kingdom
correct: And he did that which was right in the sight of the LORD, but not with a perfect heart
explanation: Amaziah observed external legal conformity, but his allegiance was fundamentally flawed by divided loyalties and lack of wholehearted devotion ('not with a perfect heart'). 2 Chronicles 25:2 (KJV) - "And he did that which was right in the sight of the LORD, but not with a perfect heart."

question: Why did King Amaziah execute the servants who had assassinated his father, yet spare their children?
opt1: Because the children were under the protection of the high priest within the temple gates
opt2: He slew not their children, but did as it is written in the law in the book of Moses, where the LORD commanded, saying, The fathers shall not die for the children, neither shall the children die for the fathers, but every man shall die for his own sin
opt3: Because the elders of Judah paid a ransom of two hundred talents of silver for their lives
opt4: Because he intended to draft their sons into his elite bodyguard of chariot archers
correct: He slew not their children, but did as it is written in the law in the book of Moses, where the LORD commanded, saying, The fathers shall not die for the children, neither shall the children die for the fathers, but every man shall die for his own sin
explanation: Amaziah scrupulously obeyed the individual responsibility mandate of Deuteronomy 24:16, refusing to execute the assassins' offspring for their parents' treason. 2 Chronicles 25:4 (KJV) - "But he slew not their children, but did as it is written in the law in the book of Moses, where the LORD commanded, saying, The fathers shall not die for the children, neither shall the children die for the fathers, but every man shall die for his own sin."

question: How large a mercenary force did Amaziah hire from northern Israel, what price did he pay, and what prophetic warning halted them?
opt1: Fifty thousand archers for fifty talents of gold; warned by Azariah that Samaria would betray him
opt2: Two hundred thousand swordsmen for two hundred talents of silver; warned by Hanani of divine wrath
opt3: He hired also an hundred thousand mighty men of valour out of Israel for an hundred talents of silver. But there came a man of God to him, saying, O king, let not the army of Israel go with thee; for the LORD is not with Israel, to wit, with all the children of Ephraim
opt4: Eighty thousand cavalrymen for one thousand talents of brass; warned by Zechariah of defeat
correct: He hired also an hundred thousand mighty men of valour out of Israel for an hundred talents of silver. But there came a man of God to him, saying, O king, let not the army of Israel go with thee; for the LORD is not with Israel, to wit, with all the children of Ephraim
explanation: Amaziah paid 100 talents of silver for 100,000 Ephraimite mercenaries; an unnamed man of God ordered him to dismiss them, declaring that Yahweh does not accompany apostate northern Israel. 2 Chronicles 25:6-7 (KJV) - "He hired also an hundred thousand mighty men of valour out of Israel for an hundred talents of silver. But there came a man of God to him, saying, O king, let not the army of Israel go with thee; for the LORD is not with Israel, to wit, with all the children of Ephraim."

question: When Amaziah protested the financial loss of the hundred talents of silver, what renowned answer did the man of God give him?
opt1: 'The spoil of the Edomites shall double thy silver in the valley of Salt'
opt2: 'Better is a little with the fear of the LORD than great treasure and trouble therewith'
opt3: 'Thy gold is perished with thee because thou didst trust in uncircumcised swords'
opt4: 'The LORD is able to give thee much more than this'
correct: 'The LORD is able to give thee much more than this'
explanation: The prophet delivered this classic assurance of divine abundance: no financial compromise or sacrifice made for covenant obedience exceeds God's capacity to restore and multiply. 2 Chronicles 25:9 (KJV) - "And Amaziah said to the man of God, But what shall we do for the hundred talents which I have given to the army of Israel? And the man of God answered, The LORD is able to give thee much more than this."

question: What total victory did Amaziah achieve over the Edomites in the Valley of Salt, and what severe execution was enacted atop the rock?
opt1: Amaziah strengthened himself, and led forth his people, and went to the valley of salt, and smote of the children of Seir ten thousand. And other ten thousand left alive did the children of Judah carry away captive, and brought them unto the top of the rock, and cast them down from the top of the rock, that they all were broken in pieces
opt2: He slew twenty thousand in battle and burned their capital fortress of Bozrah with fire
opt3: He captured fifteen thousand Edomites and made them permanent bondservants in Jerusalem
opt4: He destroyed thirty thousand warriors and forced the king of Edom to leap into the Dead Sea
correct: Amaziah strengthened himself, and led forth his people, and went to the valley of salt, and smote of the children of Seir ten thousand. And other ten thousand left alive did the children of Judah carry away captive, and brought them unto the top of the rock, and cast them down from the top of the rock, that they all were broken in pieces
explanation: Amaziah slaughtered 10,000 Edomites in combat, captured another 10,000, and executed them by casting them down from the sheer precipice of Sela (the rock). 2 Chronicles 25:11-12 (KJV) - "And Amaziah strengthened himself, and led forth his people, and went to the valley of salt, and smote of the children of Seir ten thousand. And other ten thousand left alive did the children of Judah carry away captive, and brought them unto the top of the rock, and cast them down from the top of the rock, that they all were broken in pieces."

question: What vengeful rampages were committed by the dismissed Ephraimite mercenaries while Amaziah was in Edom?
opt1: They marched to Jerusalem, broke the high gate, and stole the collection chest
opt2: The soldiers of the army which Amaziah sent back, that they should not go with him to battle, fell upon the cities of Judah, from Samaria even unto Beth-horon, and smote three thousand of them, and took much spoil
opt3: They allied with the Philistines and burned twenty grain fields across the plain of Sharon
opt4: They ambushed Amaziah's returning baggage train in the wilderness of Tekoa
correct: The soldiers of the army which Amaziah sent back, that they should not go with him to battle, fell upon the cities of Judah, from Samaria even unto Beth-horon, and smote three thousand of them, and took much spoil
explanation: Infuriated by their dismissal, the 100,000 northern mercenaries pillaged Judean towns from Samaria down to Beth-horon, slaughtering 3,000 citizens and looting spoil. 2 Chronicles 25:13 (KJV) - "But the soldiers of the army which Amaziah sent back, that they should not go with him to battle, fell upon the cities of Judah, from Samaria even unto Beth-horon, and smote three thousand of them, and took much spoil."

question: What astonishing theological absurdity did King Amaziah commit upon returning from the conquest of Edom?
opt1: He sacrificed his eldest son upon the high place of Mount Seir to celebrate his triumph
opt2: He dedicated all the gold of Edom to the temple of Baal in Samaria
opt3: He brought the gods of the children of Seir, and set them up to be his gods, and bowed down himself before them, and burned incense unto them
opt4: He carved an image of Chemosh and set it upon Bezaleel's brazen altar in Jerusalem
correct: He brought the gods of the children of Seir, and set them up to be his gods, and bowed down himself before them, and burned incense unto them
explanation: In inexplicable spiritual blindness, Amaziah adopted and worshipped the powerless deities of the very Edomites whom his own army had just annihilated. 2 Chronicles 25:14 (KJV) - "Now it came to pass, after that Amaziah was come from the slaughter of the Edomites, that he brought the gods of the children of Seir, and set them up to be his gods, and bowed down himself before them, and burned incense unto them."

question: What penetrating logical question did God's prophet ask Amaziah, and how did the king threaten him?
opt1: The prophet asked, 'Can gold save thee in the day of wrath?' and the king threw him into a pit
opt2: The prophet asked, 'Where is thy trust in the God of David?' and the king banished him to Egypt
opt3: The prophet asked, 'Shall uncircumcised idols heal Judah?' and the king put him in prison
opt4: The prophet said, 'Why hast thou sought after the gods of the people, which could not deliver their own people out of thine hand?' And the king said, 'Art thou made of the king's counsel? forbear; why shouldest thou be smitten?'
correct: The prophet said, 'Why hast thou sought after the gods of the people, which could not deliver their own people out of thine hand?' And the king said, 'Art thou made of the king's counsel? forbear; why shouldest thou be smitten?'
explanation: The prophet exposed the irrationality of worshipping gods that failed to save their own worshippers; Amaziah arrogantly silenced him under threat of execution. 2 Chronicles 25:15-16 (KJV) - "Wherefore the anger of the LORD was kindled against Amaziah, and he sent unto him a prophet, which said unto him, Why hast thou sought after the gods of the people, which could not deliver their own people out of thine hand? And it came to pass, as he talked with him, that the king said unto him, Art thou made of the king's counsel? forbear; why shouldest thou be smitten? Then the prophet forbare, and said, I know that God hath determined to destroy thee, because thou hast done this, and hast not hearkened unto my counsel."

question: What fable did King Joash of Israel send in response to Amaziah's hubristic military challenge ('let us see one another in the face')?
opt1: 'The thistle that was in Lebanon sent to the cedar that was in Lebanon, saying, Give thy daughter to my son to wife: and there passed by a wild beast that was in Lebanon, and trode down the thistle. Thou sayest, Lo, thou hast smitten the Edomites; and thine heart lifteth thee up to boast: abide now at home; why shouldest thou meddle to thine hurt ...'
opt2: 'The bramble of the mountain said unto the olive tree, Come and rule over us; and a flame devoured the bramble'
opt3: 'The wolf challenged the lion of Judah in the forest; and the hunter's trap snapped upon the wolf'
opt4: 'The reed of the brook shook before the hurricane of the desert; and the river swept it away into the sea'
correct: 'The thistle that was in Lebanon sent to the cedar that was in Lebanon, saying, Give thy daughter to my son to wife: and there passed by a wild beast that was in Lebanon, and trode down the thistle. Thou sayest, Lo, thou hast smitten the Edomites; and thine heart lifteth thee up to boast: abide now at home; why shouldest thou meddle to thine hurt ...'
explanation: Joash of Israel mocked Amaziah's inflated pride with the fable of an insignificant Lebanon thistle demanding marital alliance with a majestic cedar, only to be casually trampled by a wild beast. 2 Chronicles 25:18-19 (KJV) - "And Joash king of Israel sent to Amaziah king of Judah, saying, The thistle that was in Lebanon sent to the cedar that was in Lebanon, saying, Give thy daughter to my son to wife: and there passed by a wild beast that was in Lebanon, and trode down the thistle. Thou sayest, Lo, thou hast smitten the Edomites; and thine heart lifteth thee up to boast: abide now at home; why shouldest thou meddle to thine hurt, that thou shouldest fall, even thou, and Judah with thee?"

question: What humiliating devastation was inflicted upon Jerusalem by Joash of Israel following Amaziah's defeat at Beth-shemesh?
opt1: Joash burned the temple porch, took the ark of the covenant to Samaria, and executed all the priests
opt2: Joash brake down the wall of Jerusalem from the gate of Ephraim to the corner gate, four hundred cubits. And he took all the gold and the silver, and all the vessels that were found in the house of God with Obed-edom, and the treasures of the king's house, the hostages also, and returned to Samaria
opt3: Joash tore down all fifteen fenced cities of Rehoboam and demanded annual tribute of five hundred talents
opt4: Joash destroyed the palace of Solomon, blinded King Amaziah, and carried away ten thousand captives
correct: Joash brake down the wall of Jerusalem from the gate of Ephraim to the corner gate, four hundred cubits. And he took all the gold and the silver, and all the vessels that were found in the house of God with Obed-edom, and the treasures of the king's house, the hostages also, and returned to Samaria
explanation: Joash dismantled 400 cubits of Jerusalem's northern defensive wall, stripped the temple vessels (managed by Obed-edom's levitical line), plundered the royal palace, took hostages, and returned to Samaria. 2 Chronicles 25:23-24 (KJV) - "And Joash the king of Israel took Amaziah king of Judah ... and brought him to Jerusalem, and brake down the wall of Jerusalem from the gate of Ephraim to the corner gate, four hundred cubits. And he took all the gold and the silver, and all the vessels that were found in the house of God with Obed-edom, and the treasures of the king's house, the hostages also, and returned to Samaria."

question: How old was Uzziah when all the people of Judah crowned him king, and who was his spiritual mentor during his prosperous early years?
opt1: He was twenty years old, and was instructed by Isaiah the son of Amoz
opt2: Then all the people of Judah took Uzziah, who was sixteen years old, and made him king ... and he sought God in the days of Zechariah, who had understanding in the visions of God: and as long as he sought the LORD, God made him to prosper
opt3: He was twelve years old, and was guided by Azariah the high priest
opt4: He was eighteen years old, and was counselled by Hanani the seer
correct: Then all the people of Judah took Uzziah, who was sixteen years old, and made him king ... and he sought God in the days of Zechariah, who had understanding in the visions of God: and as long as he sought the LORD, God made him to prosper
explanation: Uzziah ascended at age 16, reigning 52 years; his prosperity was directly linked to seeking Yahweh under the inspired tutelage of Zechariah, who understood divine visions. 2 Chronicles 26:1, 5 (KJV) - "Then all the people of Judah took Uzziah, who was sixteen years old, and made him king in the room of his father Amaziah ... And he sought God in the days of Zechariah, who had understanding in the visions of God: and as long as he sought the LORD, God made him to prosper."

question: What military campaigns did Uzziah conduct against the Philistines and southern desert tribes in 2 Chronicles 26:6-7?

explanation: At age 16 (8th regnal year), Josiah commenced his personal spiritual quest; at age 20 (12th regnal year), he initiated a militant nationwide purge of pagan shrines. 2 Chronicles 34:3 (KJV) - "For in the eighth year of his reign, while he was yet young, he began to seek after the God of David his father: and in the twelfth year he began to purge Judah and Jerusalem from the high places, and the groves, and the carved images, and the molten images."

question: What two-fold prophetic oracle did Huldah proclaim regarding Jerusalem and King Josiah personally?
opt1: Jerusalem would be spared forever, while Josiah would defeat the armies of Babylon

explanation: Huldah affirmed that Judah's cumulative apostasy made judgment inevitable; however, because of Josiah's tender heart and tears, disaster was deferred until after his peaceful death. 2 Chronicles 34:24, 27-28 (KJV) - "Thus saith the LORD, Behold, I will bring evil upon this place, and upon the inhabitants thereof, even all the curses that are written in the book which they have read before the king of Judah ... Because thine heart was tender, and thou didst humble thyself before God ... opt1: The king went up into the house of the LORD, and all the men of Judah, and the inhabitants of Jerusalem, and the priests, and the Levites, and all the people, great and small: and he read in their ears all the words of the book of the covenant that was found in the house of the LORD

explanation: Josiah gathered all citizens—priests, Levites, nobles, and commoners—personally reading aloud the entirety of the recovered covenant scroll. 2 Chronicles 34:30 (KJV) - "And the king went up into the house of the LORD, and all the men of Judah, and the inhabitants of Jerusalem, and the priests, and the Levites, and all the people, great and small: and he read in their ears all the words of the book of the covenant that was found in the house of the LORD."

And all his days they departed not from following the LORD, the God of their fathers."

question: What historic instruction did King Josiah give to the Levites concerning the Ark of the Covenant in 2 Chronicles 35:3?

correct: But they mocked the messengers of God, and despised his words, and misused his prophets, until the wrath of the LORD arose against his people, till there was no remedy
explanation: The nation reached a tragic spiritual point of no return: mocking, despising, and mistreating God's prophets until divine wrath was aroused 'till there was no remedy' (ein marpe). 2 Chronicles 36:16 (KJV) - "But they mocked the messengers of God, and despised his words, and misused his prophets, until the wrath of the LORD arose against his people, till there was no remedy."

question: What merciless slaughter and destruction was inflicted upon Jerusalem by the Chaldean army under Nebuchadnezzar?
opt1: They took fifty thousand young men captive and spared the elderly priests of Aaron
opt2: Therefore he brought upon them the king of the Chaldees, who slew their young men with the sword in the house of their sanctuary, and had no compassion upon young man or maiden, old man, or him that stooped for age: he gave them all into his hand
opt3: They burned only the northern suburbs and spared the temple of Solomon
opt4: They demanded annual tribute of one thousand talents and left Zedekiah as regent
correct: Therefore he brought upon them the king of the Chaldees, who slew their young men with the sword in the house of their sanctuary, and had no compassion upon young man or maiden, old man, or him that stooped for age: he gave them all into his hand
explanation: The Chaldean invaders showed zero mercy: butchering youth inside the holy sanctuary itself, sparing neither young maiden nor feeble elder. 2 Chronicles 36:17 (KJV) - "Therefore he brought upon them the king of the Chaldees, who slew their young men with the sword in the house of their sanctuary, and had no compassion upon young man or maiden, old man, or him that stooped for age: he gave them all into his hand."

question: What ultimate physical devastation was wrought upon the city of Jerusalem and the temple of Solomon in 2 Chronicles 36:19?
opt1: They dismantled the two bronze pillars and placed an altar of Marduk in the temple
opt2: They took the roof off the oracle and converted the courts into an Assyrian garrison
opt3: And they burnt the house of God, and brake down the wall of Jerusalem, and burnt all the palaces thereof with fire, and destroyed all the goodly vessels thereof
opt4: They plundered the gold of the temple and left the walls standing for the poor of the land
correct: And they burnt the house of God, and brake down the wall of Jerusalem, and burnt all the palaces thereof with fire, and destroyed all the goodly vessels thereof
explanation: In 586 BC, Nebuzaradan burned Solomon's glorious temple to the ground, razed Jerusalem's defensive walls, incinerated all royal palaces, and demolished all valuable vessels. 2 Chronicles 36:19 (KJV) - "And they burnt the house of God, and brake down the wall of Jerusalem, and burnt all the palaces thereof with fire, and destroyed all the goodly vessels thereof."

question: What theological explanation does 2 Chronicles 36:21 give for the seventy-year duration of the Babylonian desolation?
opt1: Because seventy kings had reigned over the united kingdom of David and Solomon
opt2: Because the nation had sacrificed seventy thousand bullocks upon the high places of Baal
opt3: Because seventy false prophets had deceived King Zedekiah before the siege
opt4: To fulfil the word of the LORD by the mouth of Jeremiah, until the land had enjoyed her sabbaths: for as long as she lay desolate she kept sabbath, to fulfil threescore and ten years
correct: To fulfil the word of the LORD by the mouth of Jeremiah, until the land had enjoyed her sabbaths: for as long as she lay desolate she kept sabbath, to fulfil threescore and ten years
explanation: The 70-year Babylonian exile compensated for 490 prior years during which unfaithful Israel had violated the Leviticus 25/26 sabbatical agricultural rest laws for the land. 2 Chronicles 36:21 (KJV) - "To fulfil the word of the LORD by the mouth of Jeremiah, until the land had enjoyed her sabbaths: for as long as she lay desolate she kept sabbath, to fulfil threescore and ten years."

question: With what glorious decree of imperial restoration and return does 2 Chronicles and the entire Hebrew Old Testament canon conclude?
opt1: 'Thus saith Cyrus king of Persia, All the kingdoms of the earth hath the LORD God of heaven given me; and he hath charged me to build him an house in Jerusalem, which is in Judah. Who is there among you of all his people? The LORD his God be with him, and let him go up'
opt2: 'Thus saith Darius the king, Let no man hinder the building of the temple of Jerusalem, under penalty of death'
opt3: 'Thus saith Artaxerxes, Rebuild the walls of the city of David, and offer sacrifices for the royal family'
opt4: 'Thus saith the LORD, Behold, the virgin shall conceive and bear a son, and his name shall be Immanuel'
correct: 'Thus saith Cyrus king of Persia, All the kingdoms of the earth hath the LORD God of heaven given me; and he hath charged me to build him an house in Jerusalem, which is in Judah. Who is there among you of all his people? The LORD his God be with him, and let him go up'
explanation: 2 Chronicles closes with King Cyrus of Persia's inspired 538 BC proclamation: charging Jewish exiles to return to Jerusalem and rebuild the house of Yahweh ('let him go up'). 2 Chronicles 36:23 (KJV) - "Thus saith Cyrus king of Persia, All the kingdoms of the earth hath the LORD God of heaven given me; and he hath charged me to build him an house in Jerusalem, which is in Judah. Who is there among you of all his people? The LORD his God be with him, and let him go up."
